description: Which supplied PCS events train and score the hurricane damage curves. An event is excluded only by a rule about its loss mechanism or data coverage, never by how well it fits. backend/scripts/_event_set.py computes each metric; the notes record the physical reading.

noExposure.reason: Most of the PCS loss is where the industry book has no TIV, so the event cannot be priced.

stalled.reason: Stalled storm: the centre stayed 36+ hours within 100 nm of its strongest US landfall. Loss is driven by rainfall flooding and wind duration, which a peak-wind damage curve cannot represent (Harvey 2017 is the archetype).

outsideFootprint.reason: Most of the PCS loss is in counties outside the modelled hurricane-force wind field (inland tropical-storm-force wind, tornadoes, remnant rainfall or flooding), so the curve never sees the wind that caused it.

AL022024.name: Beryl
AL022024.mechanism: Cat 1 landfall at Matagorda Bay. Houston loss is wind: tree fall onto roofs and lines across the metro.

AL042024.name: Debby
AL042024.mechanism: Cat 1 Big Bend landfall, then a slow track over Georgia and South Carolina with extreme rainfall, and remnant flooding as far as the Northeast. Rain and flood driven.

AL062018.name: Florence
AL062018.mechanism: Stalled near Wilmington and set North Carolina's rainfall record; river and flash flooding drove the loss. The closest supplied analogue to Harvey.

AL092020.name: Isaias
AL092020.mechanism: Cat 1 North Carolina landfall, then raced up the East Coast as a tropical storm. Loss came from tropical-storm-force tree fall and tornadoes in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast.

AL092021.name: Ida
AL092021.mechanism: Cat 4 Port Fourchon landfall. Louisiana loss is wind, and ASOS winds in Orleans Parish match the model. About 28% of the loss is remnant flash flooding in NY, NJ and PA, below the exclusion threshold, so Ida stays in.

AL092022.name: Ian
AL092022.mechanism: Cat 4 Cayo Costa landfall with peninsula-wide wind. Lee and Charlotte surge is material, but 93% of the PCS loss is inside the modelled wind field and PCS excludes NFIP.

AL092024.name: Helene
AL092024.mechanism: Large, fast-moving Cat 4. Loss came from tropical-storm-force wind far inland across Georgia and the Carolinas and from Appalachian freshwater flooding.

AL112017.name: Irma
AL112017.mechanism: Cat 4 Keys and Cat 3 Marco Island landfalls with peninsula-wide wind. Loss outside the book (USVI / Puerto Rico rows) is left out of the score.

AL142018.name: Michael
AL142018.mechanism: Compact Cat 5 Mexico Beach landfall. Wind-driven; surge was local to the landfall coast.

AL142024.name: Milton
AL142024.mechanism: Cat 3 Siesta Key landfall. Wind, plus the tornado outbreak ahead of landfall.

AL152017.name: Maria
AL152017.mechanism: Puerto Rico and USVI, where the industry book carries no TIV.

AL192020.name: Sally
AL192020.mechanism: Crawled ashore at Gulf Shores at walking pace, with extreme rainfall over Baldwin County and Pensacola. Rain flooding and long-duration wind, not peak wind.

AL262020.name: Delta
AL262020.mechanism: Landed about 12 miles east of Laura's landfall six weeks later, on Laura-damaged and tarped roofs, so the PCS split between the two events is confounded. Most of the loss was inland, outside the modelled field.

AL282020.name: Zeta
AL282020.mechanism: Very fast-moving Cat 3 in southeast Louisiana. Tropical-storm-force wind was carried far inland across Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia and the Carolinas.
